title: Reduced contrast volume in coronary CT angiography: effects on coronary attenuation
authors: Perihan Adel Ali El Naqeeb; Medhat Wahba Shafaa; Ayman Mohamed Ibrahim; Ahmed Hamdy; Ahmed Shehata Ismail
journal: The Egyptian Journal of Radiology and Nuclear Medicine
abstract: Abstract Background Coronary CT angiography (CCTA) requires intravenous iodinated contrast to achieve diagnostic intraluminal opacification. Because reducing the contrast volume administered per examination is an exposure-reduction strategy of practical interest, institutions have explored lower-volume protocols; whether attenuation can be preserved above the diagnostic threshold under real-world, non-randomized implementation is not well documented outside research settings. Methods This retrospective, single-centre, non-concurrent before-and-after protocol-implementation study was conducted at Radiology Center (January 2023–December 2024). From 200 CCTA examinations initially identified from radiology reports as potentially eligible, 106 were excluded (44 body weight >120 kg; 12 beta-blocker administered; 27 coronary calcification/calcium scoring without significant stenosis; 23 motion artefact), leaving 94 CT-angiographically normal examinations: 51 under the standard (pre-reduction) protocol and 43 under the reduced-volume (post-reduction) protocol. All examinations used a third-generation dual-source CT scanner (Siemens SOMATOM Force) with automated tube-voltage selection (CARE kV) and tube-current modulation (CARE Dose4D), retrospective ECG gating, and a 32-cm scan length. Omnipaque 350 mgI/mL was administered by power injector with bolus tracking (ascending aorta ROI, 90 HU trigger, 5 s post-trigger delay). Intraluminal attenuation was measured by a single reader in the left main trunk (LMT) and proximal right coronary artery (RCA); no inter- or intra-observer reproducibility assessment was performed. Distributions were assessed with the Shapiro–Wilk test; normally distributed variables were compared with the independent-samples (Welch) t-test and non-normally distributed variables with the Mann–Whitney U test. A multivariable linear model examined coronary attenuation as a function of protocol epoch, kVp, body weight, heart rate, and iodine delivery rate. Results Contrast volume fell from 63.4 ± 7.3 mL to 49.0 ± 8.0 mL (median 60 [IQR 60–65] vs 45 [45–52.5] mL), a 22.8% reduction (Mann–Whitney p < 0.001), with a corresponding 22.8% reduction in iodine mass (22.20 ± 2.56 vs 17.13 ± 2.79 gI). Iodine delivery rate was essentially unchanged (1.69 ± 0.14 vs 1.69 ± 0.14 gI/s; p = 0.91). Mean LMT attenuation decreased from 520.4 ± 93.6 HU to 451.9 ± 90.7 HU (− 13.2%; t-test p < 0.001) and mean RCA attenuation from 500.2 ± 107.1 HU to 418.1 ± 89.3 HU (− 16.4%; Mann–Whitney p < 0.001). At the per-patient level, 41/43 post-reduction examinations (95.3%; exact 95% CI 84.2–99.4%) reached ≥ 300 HU at the LMT and 39/43 (90.7%; 95% CI 77.9–97.4%) at the RCA; 4/43 examinations, therefore, fell below the SCCT diagnostic threshold at the RCA and 2/43 at the LMT. In the multivariable model, protocol epoch remained independently associated with lower attenuation after adjustment for kVp, weight, heart rate, and iodine delivery rate (LMT: β = − 75.7 HU, 95% CI − 111.6 to − 39.8, p < 0.001; RCA: β = − 87.8 HU, 95% CI − 128.0 to − 47.7, p < 0.001). Mean DLP was 1158.2 ± 637.4 mGy·cm (pre) versus 1072.1 ± 530.6 mGy·cm (post), a non-significant 7.4% difference (Mann–Whitney p = 0.71); the reduction in DLP standard deviation (16.8%) corresponds to an estimated 30.7% reduction in variance, which was not statistically significant (Levene’s test p = 0.24). No renal function or image-quality metric was measured. Conclusion A reduced-volume contrast protocol lowered administered contrast volume and total iodine mass by 22.8% while iodine delivery rate was maintained. Mean coronary attenuation remained above 300 HU in both groups, but a per-patient minority of post-reduction examinations fell below this threshold, particularly at the RCA. Radiation-dose differences were a co-temporal secondary observation and are not attributable to the contrast protocol. Renal outcomes were not assessed, and the findings should not be interpreted as evidence of nephroprotection or as a formal non-inferiority result.

title: Updated systematic review and meta-analysis comparing Myval versus Sapien 3 transcatheter heart valves in severe aortic stenosis: focus on early and one-year mortality
authors: Lin Yang; Guisong Yu; Mingchen Pan; Yandong Liu; Yuxi Zhu; Mengyu Zhang; Haigen Yu; Zhaohui Pei
abstract: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is a guideline-recommended treatment for severe aortic stenosis (AS). While the balloon-expandable Edwards Sapien 3 valve has long been the benchmark, the newer Myval valve has emerged as a potential alternative. Comparative data on mid-term survival, specifically one-year all-cause mortality, are lacking but crucial for clinical evaluation. This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesised direct comparative evidence on the Myval versus Sapien 3 valves in patients undergoing TAVI, searching PubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Central up to November 2025. The primary outcomes included all-cause mortality within 30 days and 1 year. Secondary outcomes were 30-day safety events and hemodynamic parameters. Five studies (n = 2771) were included. The pooled analysis indicated no statistical difference in 30-day mortality (RR: 1.05, 95% CI: 0.53–2.07; p = 0.89; I2=0%) or in one-year all-cause mortality (RR: 0.93, 95% CI: 0.64–1.35; p = 0.70; I2=0%). Rates of stroke, major bleeding, pacemaker implantation, and other 30-day complications were also comparable (all p > 0.05). Hemodynamically, the Myval valve was superior at 30 days, with a lower mean gradient (MD: −2.37, 95% CI: −3.45 to −1.30; p < 0.0001) and larger effective orifice area (MD: 0.26, 95% CI: 0.17–0.35; p < 0.00001). Available one-year data from two randomised trials indicated this hemodynamic benefit was sustained. This updated meta-analysis demonstrates that the newer Myval valve offers comparable early safety and one-year survival to the established Sapien 3 valve, with superior and sustained hemodynamic performance. These findings support its role as a safe and effective alternative in the TAVI landscape.

title: Evaluating the impact of passive driver position on image consistency and repeatability in 3.0T cardiac magnetic resonance elastography
authors: Jun Wang; Shutian An; Zhen Wang; Zichen Hu; Yueyue Zhang; Daiwang Jia; Yong Cheng; Yang Xiang; Ruan Fang; Peiyang Zheng; Zijun Zheng; Zhanglei Li; Yewen Jiang; Yongqiang Yu; Ren Zhao; Xiaohu Li
abstract: Background Cardiac magnetic resonance elastography (MRE) is a non-invasive technique that quantifies myocardial stiffness by tracking shear wave propagation through the heart. Shear waves are generated externally and delivered to the thorax through a passive driver placed on the chest. Passive driver position is a critical yet underexplored determinant of measurement quality. Purpose To compare two passive driver positions in 3.0 T cardiac MRE — the apical surface projection (ASP) and the left lateral chest wall (LCW) — and to determine which yields more reliable left ventricular (LV) myocardial stiffness measurements. Methods Twenty-three healthy volunteers (mean age 43.0 ± 17.0 years; 14 men, 9 women) underwent two cardiac MRE acquisitions, with the passive driver placed first at the ASP and then at the LCW. LV myocardial stiffness and the octahedral shear strain signal-to-noise ratio (OSS-SNR) were measured at both positions. Differences between positions were analyzed using paired t-tests with Cohen's d . Inter- and intra-observer reproducibility were assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC) and Bland–Altman analysis. Results Myocardial stiffness was significantly lower at the ASP than at the LCW (9.0 ± 1.7 kPa vs. 14.7 ± 3.0 kPa; mean difference −5.8 kPa, 95% CI −7.2 to −4.3; P < 0.001 ; Cohen's d = − 1.73 ). OSS-SNR was significantly higher at the ASP (1.72 ± 0.48 vs. 1.25 ± 0.29; P < 0.001 ; Cohen's d = 0.85 ). At the ASP, stiffness measurements demonstrated excellent intra- and inter-observer agreement, with ICCs of 0.962 and 0.963, respectively. At the LCW, stiffness measurements demonstrated good inter-observer agreement and excellent intra-observer agreement, with ICCs of 0.839 and 0.914, respectively. Conclusion Passive driver placement at the ASP resulted in significantly higher OSS-SNR and superior reproducibility for LV myocardial stiffness measurements compared with LCW placement. Therefore, the ASP should be considered the preferred driver position for cardiac MRE in clinical and research settings.

title: Selective conduction differences in children with isolated bicuspid aortic valve
authors: Uğur Saraç; Ayşe Büşra Paydaş; Mehmet Babür; Mehmet Burhan Oflaz; Tamer Baysal; Fatih Şap
abstract: Objective: Bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) is one of the most common congenital heart defects, yet the electrocardiographic features of isolated BAV in children have not been well characterized. We aimed to evaluate electrocardiographic parameters in pediatric patients with isolated BAV and to investigate whether early electrical changes are detectable before overt valve dysfunction. Materials and Methods: In this retrospective case-control study, 30 children with isolated and hemodynamically uncomplicated BAV were compared with 32 age- and sex-matched healthy controls. Via 12-lead surface electrocardiography, P wave parameters, QT and QTc intervals, QRS duration, axis measurements, and the QRS-T angle were assessed by two blinded investigators. For the ECG parameters, correction for multiple comparisons was applied with the Benjamini-Hochberg method. Results: The study included 30 children with BAV and 32 controls; median age was 142.5 versus 141.5 months, and male sex was present in 70.0% versus 75.0%, respectively. After correction for multiple comparisons, only the minimum duration of the P wave (q=0.005) and the dispersion of the P wave (q=0.008) showed significant differences between the groups; P minimum duration was higher and P wave dispersion was lower in the BAV group. No difference was found between the groups in the PR interval, QRS duration, the parameters of repolarization, and axis measurements. In the BAV group, aortic Z-scores were higher despite preserved systolic function of the left ventricle, and the left ventricular mass index did not reach statistical significance (p=0.058). Conclusion: Isolated pediatric BAV is associated with selective electrocardiographic changes at the level of atrial conduction, in the absence of a hemodynamic burden, while ventricular conduction and repolarization are not affected at this stage.

title: Case Report: staged segment-specific open and endovascular treatment of chronic post-dissection aortic disease with descending thoracic and giant infrarenal aneurysmal components
authors: Azat Chinaliyev; Mukhammejan Orazbay; Gulinur Chinaliyeva; Didar Khassenov; Tokan Sultanaliyev; Irlan Sagandykov; Aktolkyn Daumen
abstract: Background Contemporary management of chronic post-dissection aortic disease includes open repair, thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) with or without adjunctive false-lumen occlusion, fenestrated/branched endovascular repair, and staged open-endovascular strategies. Selection depends on anatomy, rupture risk, malperfusion, physiological reserve, and device availability. Case presentation A 56-year-old woman with body mass index 47.2 kg/m 2 and major cardiometabolic comorbidity presented with progressive abdominal pulsation. CTA demonstrated chronic Stanford type B/DeBakey III dissection with descending thoracic aneurysmal degeneration to 52.7 mm, a dominant symptomatic infrarenal aneurysmal component measuring approximately 11–12 cm, bilateral common iliac involvement, and residual paravisceral dissection without treatment-triggering enlargement or malperfusion. No Crawford extent was assigned because complete longitudinal centerline imaging was unavailable. Stage I comprised transperitoneal open aorto-bi-iliac reconstruction. After 118 days, elective morphology-driven zone 2 TEVAR was performed to cover the reported proximal entry region and reduce antegrade false-lumen inflow. Intentional left subclavian artery (LSA) coverage without prophylactic revascularization was followed by symptomatic subclavian steal requiring unplanned carotid-subclavian bypass. Results No perioperative death, stroke, spinal cord ischemia, bowel ischemia, myocardial infarction, acute kidney injury, graft thrombosis, prosthetic infection, or access complication occurred. At latest follow-up, the patient was asymptomatic and all reconstructions were patent. Conclusion This case illustrates competing priorities in segment-specific management of chronic post-dissection aortic disease. The unequivocal indication for urgent infrarenal repair contrasted with discretionary pre-emptive thoracic intervention below the conventional diameter threshold. The LSA-related complication emphasizes prophylactic LSA preservation/revascularization, spinal collateral planning, and lifelong surveillance of the untreated paravisceral segment after previous abdominal aortic reconstruction.

title: Association between mitral annular calcification and coronary stenosis severity in preoperative fracture patients
authors: Yanming Li; Junhong Zhou; Shaorong Lu; Ziwei Sun; Ying Gao; Meng Li
abstract: Mitral annular calcification (MAC) has been associated with coronary artery disease in population-based studies, but its relationship with preoperative coronary artery stenosis (CAS) severity, particularly in elderly orthopedic fracture patients, remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the association between MAC and CAS severity, and to determine whether MAC provides incremental discriminatory value beyond traditional risk factors. We retrospectively analyzed 191 consecutive orthopedic fracture patients who underwent both transthoracic echocardiography for MAC assessment and coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) for preoperative cardiac risk stratification between December 1, 2022, and December 31, 2022. When CCTA revealed a stenosis judged to require intervention (typically > 70% diameter reduction, or > 50% with high-risk features), the patient was referred for invasive coronary angiography (ICA). CAS was graded on an ordinal scale (0–IV) and also dichotomized at three cutoffs: any stenosis (grade ≥ I), obstructive stenosis (grade ≥ III), and occlusive disease (grade IV). Ordinal logistic regression was used to assess the association between MAC and CAS grade, with progressive adjustment for covariates across four model specifications: Model A (age, sex, hypertension), Model B (Model A + diabetes, hyperlipidemia, aortic valve calcification), Model C (12 exploratory variables), and a modified Revised Cardiac Risk Index (RCRI) model (age, sex, MAC, exploratory modified RCRI-like score). Model A served as the primary analysis, while Models B, C, and the modified RCRI model were conducted as sensitivity analyses to assess the robustness of the association. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was used to quantify the incremental discriminatory value of MAC beyond traditional risk factors. MAC was present in 77 patients (40.3%), with prevalence increasing from 12.0% in Grade 0 to 95.8% in Grade IV. In ordinal logistic regression, MAC was the factor most strongly associated with higher stenosis grade across all models: Model A OR 12.56 (95% CI 6.11–25.84, p < 0.001) and modified RCRI model OR 11.73 (95% CI 5.69–24.17, p < 0.001). Consistent results were obtained in exploratory sensitivity analyses (Models B and C). For the binary outcome of obstructive stenosis (Grade ≥ III), adding MAC to the baseline clinical model (age, sex, hypertension) improved the AUC from 0.73 (95% CI 0.64–0.81) to 0.86 (95% CI 0.80–0.92), Δ=+0.13 (DeLong test with bootstrap, p = 0.001). The modified RCRI-like model achieved an AUC of 0.88 (95% CI 0.82–0.93). The MAC-CAS association persisted in the CCTA-only subgroup ( n = 152, OR 4.35–6.32, all p < 0.001), suggesting that the association is not entirely driven by referral to invasive angiography, although referral selection bias for CCTA remains. Factors independently associated with MAC included aortic valve calcification (OR 7.79), hypertension (OR 3.27), male (OR 2.49) and age (OR 1.04 per year). MAC demonstrated a strong and independent association with CAS severity in this selected cohort of elderly orthopedic fracture patients. A simplified four-variable model combining MAC and the exploratory modified RCRI-like score achieved an AUC of 0.88. However, these findings are hypothesis-generating and do not establish MAC as a clinical prediction tool. Given that echocardiography is routinely performed in this population, MAC assessment requires no additional imaging or cost. Importantly, these findings are derived from a highly selected cohort—only 12% of screened fracture patients were included—and should be considered specific to patients referred for advanced cardiovascular imaging. The conclusions do not apply to the broader population of patients undergoing urgent orthopedic surgery. Prospective multi-center studies in unselected fracture populations with hard clinical endpoints are warranted to validate these findings.

title: Impact of CYP2C9 and VKORC1 polymorphisms on warfarin dose and anticoagulation response in cardiac valve replacement patients in Erbil, Iraq
authors: Zeina Mahmood; Kawa Fareq Dizaye
abstract: Background and objective: Warfarin is the primary anticoagulant used in patients undergoing heart valve replacement surgery. Genetic variations in the CYP2C9 and VKORC1 (Vitamin K Epoxide Reductase Complex Subunit 1) genes have a significant impact on warfarin metabolism and sensitivity. However, there are limited studies on these variants in the Iraqi population. The purpose of this study was to assess the impact of the single-nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) VKORC1 -1639 G>A, CYP2C9*2, and CYP2C9*3 on anticoagulation response, time to reach therapeutic International Normalised Ratio (INR), and warfarin dosage requirements in patients undergoing heart valve replacement surgery. Methods: Fifty patients (34 Kurdish, 16 Arab) participated in a prospective observational study in Erbil, Iraq, from October 2024 to March 2025. Real-time PCR was used for genotyping. INR values, warfarin dosing, and the time in days from the first day of warfarin treatment after surgery until reaching the therapeutic INR (2–3) were recorded. Results: CYP2C9 *1/*1 was the most common genotype. VKORC1 genotype frequencies differed significantly between Kurdish and Arab patients. Warfarin maintenance dose varied significantly by CYP2C9 (p=0.017) and VKORC1 (p=0.04) genotype. Patients with CYP2C9 *2/*3 required the lowest dose (7 mg/week). CYP2C9 genotype correlated with time to therapeutic INR (p=0.043), while VKORC1 genotype did not. Conclusion: The CYP2C9 and VKORC1 polymorphisms found in the studied population require lower warfarin dosages in Iraqi patients who have undergone heart valve replacement. These results demonstrate the importance of genotype-guided warfarin dosing in enhancing safety and efficacy, especially in genetically diverse populations such as Iraq.

title: The effect of different exercise modalities on the maximal left ventricular outflow tract gradient in patients with obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
authors: Maximilian Nicolas Möbius-Winkler; Andreas Hagendorff; Stephan Stöbe; Michael Gaier; Alexander Kögel; Marios Antoniadis; Ulrich Laufs; Michael Metze; Karsten Lenk; Joscha Kandels
abstract: BACKGROUND: Assessment of maximally provoked LVOT obstruction (LVOTO) guides treatment decisions in obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM). Guidelines recommend various maneuvers, with exercise stress echocardiography (ESE) as the preferred method if others fail. Comparative data are limited. Therefore, in this prospective study, 20 patients with obstructive HCM underwent transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) with continuous wave Doppler measuring LVOT gradients at rest, during the Valsalva maneuver, handgrip exercise at 30% and 50% of maximal hand force, squats, and bicycle ESE, with the aim of comparing commonly used maneuvers and evaluating handgrip exercise as a potential alternative for eliciting LVOTO. RESULTS: The mean resting LVOT gradient was 38.9 ± 31.4 mmHg. Handgrip exercise caused no significant change of LVOT gradients. In contrast, gradients increased markedly during the Valsalva maneuver (98.9 ± 52.8 mmHg), squats (120.3 ± 68.8 mmHg), and bicycle ESE (83.4 ± 43.3 mmHg; p < 0.001 vs. rest). There was no significant difference between Valsalva, squats, and ESE (p = NS). Squats induced the maximal gradient in 50% of patients. Performance time was significantly shorter for the Valsalva maneuver (15 s) and squats (1 min 23 s ± 28 s) than for bicycle ESE (15 min 54 s ± 5 min 46 s; p < 0.01). CONCLUSION: The Valsalva maneuver, squats, and bicycle ESE are equally effective in provoking LVOTO, whereas handgrip exercise is not. Given their simplicity, low cost, and shorter testing time, squats may serve as a practical adjunct to the Valsalva maneuver for LVOT gradient provocation in routine clinical assessment of obstructive HCM. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: German Clinical Trials Register (ID: DRKS00034473).

title: RBMS1 Contributes to Early Arteriovenous Fistula Neointimal Remodeling Through Modulation of VSMC Phenotypic Responses
authors: Zongda Li; Chengwei Zhang; Xinying Yu; Shuang Yao; Yiting Lai; Xiaozhu Sun; Yao Zhao; Xiaoyu Lan; Tingting Hu; Wenjin Li; Zhenzhen Ma; Huimin Ma; Zihan Wang; Haihai Liang; Jundong Jiao
abstract: Arteriovenous fistula (AVF) creation initiates stage-dependent remodeling of the venous outflow tract. Neointimal hyperplasia is a common component of this response, but its post-transcriptional regulation remains unclear. Here, analyses of human AVF datasets and tissue specimens characterized RNA-binding motif single-stranded interacting protein 1 (RBMS1) expression in postoperative AVFs, whereas a day-14 mouse AVF model and cultured vascular smooth muscle cells (VSMCs) were used to investigate its role in early neointimal remodeling. Smooth muscle-targeted RBMS1 overexpression aggravated neointimal formation, whereas conditional RBMS1 deletion attenuated it in murine AVFs. In cultured VSMCs, RBMS1 overexpression enhanced proliferation, migration, and the transition from contractile to synthetic marker expression, whereas RBMS1 silencing produced the opposite effects. Mechanistically, RBMS1 bound myelin protein zero-like 1 (MPZL1) mRNA and promoted exon 5 skipping, generating the MPZL1-Δ5 isoform. MPZL1-Δ5 overexpression reproduced selected RBMS1-associated VSMC responses and increased neointimal hyperplasia in vivo, including in RBMS1-deficient mice. MPZL1-Δ5 further interacted with GTPase-activating protein SH3 domain-binding protein 1 (G3BP1) and enhanced protein kinase B (AKT) activation, whereas G3BP1 silencing attenuated RBMS1- or MPZL1-Δ5-induced VSMC responses. Together, these findings identify the RBMS1-MPZL1-Δ5-G3BP1-AKT pathway as an important VSMC-associated mechanism contributing to neointimal remodeling during the early postoperative phase of experimental AVFs.

title: Spinal Anesthesia: Techniques And Complications
authors: Muhammad Omar Zidan; Agus Rukmana; Jacky Desfriadi
journal: International Journal of Health Engineering and Technology
abstract: Spinal anesthesia is a neuraxial technique involving the injection of local anesthetic into the subarachnoid space to produce reversible sensory, motor, and sympathetic blockade. It is widely used for surgeries below the umbilicus, including lower abdominal, pelvic, perineal, lower extremity, and obstetric procedures. Despite its advantages, such as rapid onset and effective anesthesia, complications may include hypotension, bradycardia, high or total spinal, post-dural puncture headache (PDPH), neurological complications, hematoma, and infection. Therefore, appropriate patient selection, procedural technique, monitoring, and complication prevention are essential. This final assignment employed a literature review by examining relevant sources on spinal anesthesia, including anatomy and physiology, indications and contraindications, patient and equipment preparation, anesthetic agents and adjuvants, techniques, factors affecting block spread, monitoring, complications, prevention, and recent developments. The literature was descriptively analyzed to provide an overview of the clinical application and safety of spinal anesthesia. Spinal anesthesia is effective for various surgical procedures, with outcomes influenced by patient characteristics, drug selection, puncture technique, and anesthetic spread. Bupivacaine is commonly used, with anesthetic agents and adjuvants selected according to the desired block characteristics. Prevention of complications includes proper patient evaluation, atraumatic puncture, ultrasound guidance when appropriate, antithrombotic management, hemodynamic monitoring, and aseptic techniques. Recent developments include pencil-point needles, neuraxial ultrasound, intrathecal adjuvants, and unilateral spinal anesthesia. Safe spinal anesthesia requires appropriate preparation, technique, drug selection, monitoring, and early recognition and prevention of complications.

title: Personalized Contrast Dosing in TAVI: Weight-Adjusted Contrast Exposure and Renal Biomarker Changes in High-Risk Patients
authors: Shu Fon Muna
abstract: Article title: Personalized Contrast Dosing in TAVI: Weight-Adjusted Contrast Exposure and Renal Biomarker Changes in High-Risk Patients. AbstractBackground/Objectives: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is an established alternative to surgical aortic valve replacement in patients with severe aortic stenosis and high surgical risk. Renal dysfunction following TAVI remains clinically relevant, particularly in patients with baseline chronic kidney disease and systemic comorbidities. This study evaluated renal outcomes following TAVI and explored associations between weight-adjusted contrast volume and renal biomarker changes.Methods: This retrospective cohort study included 425 consecutive patients who underwent TAVI between 2018 and 2021. Following predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria, 371 patients with complete data were included in the final analysis. Change in serum creatinine and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) after TAVI were analyzed. Spearman’s rank correlation analysis was used to evaluate associations between renal biomarker changes and contrast-related variables, age, and body mass index (BMI). Results: Equal or lower post-procedural creatinine values were observed in 235/371 patients (63.3%), while equal or higher eGFR values were observed in 238/371 patients (64.2%). Weight-adjusted contrast volume demonstrated weak but statistically significant associations with changes in creatinine (rS = 0.149, p = 0.005) and eGFR (rS = -0.148, p = 0.005) while Contrast agent volume alone showed no correlation. Sex-related differences in renal biomarker changes were not statistically significant, (creatinine (p = 0.058) and eGFR change (p = 0.238)). Conclusions: Renal outcomes following TAVI appear multifactorial and are not solely determined by contrast exposure. Although the observed associations between weight-adjusted contrast volume and renal biomarker changes were weak, the findings support individualized contrast assessment and management in high-risk TAVI populations. These exploratory findings should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating rather than evidence of direct contrast causality or renal protection.

title: Arterial tortuosity syndrome with coronary artery involvement in a middle-aged female: A case report
authors: Prinsa Shrestha; Amin Shah; Saroj GC; Niraj Kumar Sharma; Aditya Mahaseth; Sanjaya Kumar Shrestha
abstract: Arterial tortuosity syndrome (ATS) is a rare autosomal recessive connective-tissue arteriopathy characterized by diffuse elongation and tortuosity of large and medium-sized arteries. Although it is typically diagnosed during childhood, adult presentation may occur and can be overlooked when overt connective-tissue manifestations are absent; coronary involvement is uncommon but clinically important. A 41-year-old woman presented with a two-week history of exertional substernal chest pain and dyspnea. CT coronary angiography demonstrated marked tortuosity of the left main coronary artery with focal kinking approximately 6.8 mm from its origin and 40–45% luminal stenosis (CAD-RADS 2). Contrast-enhanced CT angiography of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis demonstrated generalized arterial elongation and marked tortuosity involving the thoracic aorta, supra-aortic branches, and abdominal aortic branches, together with early branching of the main pulmonary artery, without aneurysm, dissection, or intramural hematoma. Conventional coronary angiography was technically unsuccessful because of severe arterial tortuosity, with unsuccessful catheter advancement and coronary engagement despite radial and subsequent femoral access. The overall clinical and imaging findings were highly suggestive of ATS with coronary involvement, although molecular genetic confirmation was not available. The patient was managed conservatively with vascular risk-factor optimization and structured follow-up, with symptomatic improvement at one month. This case highlights that ATS may present in adulthood with coronary artery tortuosity and focal kinking and emphasizes the importance of recognizing diffuse multi-territory arterial tortuosity on CT. Comprehensive vascular imaging can establish a strong radiological suspicion of ATS, identify coronary involvement and procedural challenges, and guide surveillance even when genetic confirmation is unavailable.

title: PCI in TAVI candidates with coronary artery disease: impact of revascularization strategy and timing on outcomes
authors: Ricardo Micael Mendes Morais Carvalheiro; Miguel Marques Antunes; Francisco Barbas de Albuquerque; Bárbara Teixeira; A Grazina; Pedro Brás; Tiago Mendonça; Luis Almeida Morais; Inês Rodrigues; Tiago Pereira da Silva; Rúben Ramos; António José Fiarresga; Rui Cruz Ferreira; Duarte Cacela
abstract: Introduction and objectives: Coronary artery disease (CAD) is common in candidates for transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI), but the benefits and optimal timing of periprocedural percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) remain uncertain.We evaluated the prognostic impact and timing of periprocedural PCI in TAVI candidates with significant CAD.Methods: Retrospective study of patients with severe symptomatic aortic stenosis and significant CAD who underwent TAVI at a Portuguese tertiary center between 2009 and 2023.Patients received planned periprocedural PCI (≤ 6 months before or concomitant with TAVI) or optimal medical therapy.The primary endpoints were 24-month overall and cardiovascular survival.Secondary outcomes included 30-day mortality, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE), life-threatening bleeding, periprocedural laboratory changes, and unplanned revascularization.Furthermore, propensity score matching was performed.PCI timing (before vs concomitant with TAVI) was compared.Results: Of 174 patients, 80 (46.0%) underwent PCI and 94 (54.0%) received optimal medical therapy.At 24 months, overall and cardiovascular survival were comparable (19.5 vs 18.2 months; P = .586and 22.3 vs 20.8 months; P = .182,respectively).In the propensity-matched cohort (n = 108), PCI was not associated with a survival benefit (all-cause mortality: HR, 0.98; P = .950;cardiovascular mortality: HR, 1.40; P = .610).Thirty-day mortality, MACE, bleeding, and revascularization rates did not differ significantly between groups.Among patients undergoing PCI, concomitant PCI required more contrast and longer procedures.Although the unadjusted analysis suggested lower 24-month all-cause survival with concomitant PCI, this association did not persist after multivariable adjustment.Conclusions: In TAVI candidates with obstructive CAD, planned periprocedural PCI did not improve survival compared with optimal medical therapy, even after propensity score matching.PCI timing was not associated with differences in clinical outcomes, although concomitant procedures increased procedural burden.

title: Associations of Mild or Trace Valvular Abnormalities With Cardiac Remodeling in Older Adults: The ARIC Study
authors: Yumin Gao; Jonathan Rubin; Susan C. Cheng; Lena M. Mathews; Ajay Jayant Kirtane; Ron Cornelis Hoogeveen; Christie Mitchell Ballantyne; Elizabeth Selvin; Martin B. Leon; Josef Coresh; Scott David Solomon; Amil M. Shah; Kunihiro Matsushita
journal: Journal of the American Heart Association
abstract: Background The impact of mild/trace valvular abnormalities on cardiac remodeling is not well understood, despite their association with poor cardiovascular outcomes. Methods Using data from 4684 participants in the ARIC (Atherosclerosis Risk in Communities) Study (2011–2013), aged 66 to 90 years, we examined cross‐sectional associations of mild/trace valvular abnormalities (aortic stenosis, aortic regurgitation, and mitral regurgitation) with cardiac parameters using multivariable linear regression models. Cardiac parameters included cardiac structure (eg, left ventricular mass index), systolic function (eg, ejection fraction), diastolic function, and biomarkers (eg, high‐sensitivity cardiac troponin T). Results The prevalence was 4.3% for mild aortic stenosis, 10.9% for mild/trace aortic regurgitation, and 44.7% for mild/trace mitral regurgitation. Mitral regurgitation showed the most consistent associations with cardiac measures (left ventricular mass index 5.48 g/m 2 [95% CI, 4.38–6.57 g/m 2 ]; ejection fraction –1.92% [95% CI, −2.29% to −1.54%]; high‐sensitivity cardiac troponin T 0.08 log ng/L [95% CI, 0.05–0.12 log ng/L]). Aortic stenosis was associated with impaired ventricular filling (Ratio of early transmitral flow velocity to early diastolic mitral annular velocity (E/e’) lateral ratio 2.00 [95% CI, 1.48–2.53]) and elevated biomarkers (high‐sensitivity cardiac troponin T 0.17 ng/L [95% CI, 0.09–0.25 ng/L]), whereas aortic regurgitation was associated with worsened cardiac structure (left ventricular mass index 3.52 [95% CI, 1.76–5.28] g/m 2 ) and systolic dysfunction (ejection fraction −1.54% [95% CI, −2.14% to −0.94%]). A dose–response relationship was also observed between the number of total abnormalities and all cardiac parameters examined. Conclusions Mild/trace mitral regurgitation was most consistently associated with all cardiac parameters examined. Aortic stenosis was associated with elevated E/e’ lateral ratio and high‐sensitivity cardiac troponin T, whereas aortic regurgitation was associated with worsening in cardiac structure and ejection fraction. Our study supports the possibility of pathophysiological contributions of these mild/trace valvular abnormalities.

title: Limb Salvage Outcomes Following Endovascular Revascularization for Peripheral Artery Disease in a Southern Indian Population: A Single-Center Retrospective Study
authors: Sibasankar Dalai; Aravind Varma Datla; Ananta Rao Baratam; Mohan Rao Ambati; Rajasekhar Donkada; Surendra N Velamala; Chittaranjan N Vangapandu; Rama Sravya Saripalli; Merlin A Abraham
abstract: BackgroundPeripheral artery disease (PAD), particularly chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI), is associated with a high risk of limb loss and significant morbidity.Endovascular therapy (ET) has emerged as a minimally invasive alternative to surgical revascularization, especially in high-risk patients and those with comorbidities.This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of ET in achieving limb salvage in a Southern Indian population. Materials and methodsThis retrospective observational study was conducted at a tertiary vascular care center and included 142 patients with symptomatic PAD who underwent endovascular intervention between July 2023 and June 2025.Clinical severity and lesion complexity were assessed using the Rutherford classification and the TransAtlantic Inter-Society Consensus II (TASC II) classification, respectively.The primary endpoint was limb salvage at one year, defined as freedom from major amputation.Secondary endpoints included technical success, restenosis, and procedure-related complications. ResultsThe study population was predominantly male (87.3%) with a mean age of 61.11 ± 12.90 years.Most patients (78.1%) presented with CLTI.Technical success was achieved in 87.3% of procedures.At one-year follow-up, limb salvage was achieved in 95.8% of patients, with major amputation occurring in 4.2% and minor amputation in 9.1%.Restenosis was observed in 14.7% of cases.Procedure-related complications were infrequent and mostly minor, with one all-cause death during follow-up. ConclusionsET is a safe and effective modality for limb salvage in PAD patients, particularly in populations with a high prevalence of diabetes and advanced disease at presentation.High limb salvage rates can be achieved even in cohorts predominantly comprising patients with CLTI, supporting an endovascular-first approach in appropriately selected patients.

title: Heart-to-kidney signal by extracellular vesicles promotes kidney injury in cardiorenal syndrome
authors: Morad Asadi; Carlos G. Santos‐Gallego; Maria Anastasiadou; Jakob Christoph Voran; Benedikt-Johannes Becker; Hunter W. Korsmo; Jianhua Li; Juan Antonio Requena-Ibáñez; Brian Fardman; Vasile Pavlov; Yansui Li; Gohar Mosoyan; Yasmine Ammi; Weibin Zhou; Chengguo Wei; Steve Coca; Yongjie Yang; Zhengzi Yi; Weijia Zhang; Kiyotake Ishikawa; Tarik M. Bozoglu; Vivette Denise D’Agati; Juan J. Badimon; John C He; Gianluigi Condorelli; Christian Kupatt; Derk Frank; Lewis Kaufman
abstract: AIMS: Cardiorenal syndrome type-1 (CRS1), defined as acute kidney injury occurring in the setting of acute cardiac illness, is associated with substantial morbidity and mortality. Our objective was to determine whether extracellular vesicles (EVs) derived from the injured heart localize to the kidneys and contribute to renal injury in CRS1, and to elucidate mechanisms by which cardiac-derived EVs mediate kidney damage. METHODS AND RESULTS: Using cardiomyocyte-specific EV reporter mice, we characterized the release of cardiac-derived EVs and their biodistribution to the kidneys. Acute myocardial infarction increased circulating levels of these EVs and enhanced their uptake by proximal tubular epithelial cells. To directly assess their impact on the kidney, EVs derived from cardiomyocytes cultured under normoxic (N-EV) or hypoxic (H-EV) conditions were injected into the renal arteries of wild-type mice. H-EV, but not N-EV, induced proximal tubular epithelial cell injury and worsening of kidney function. To identify EV biomarkers, we performed proteomic profiling of cargo from N-EV and H-EV, and validated the muscle-specific protein TRIM72 as a biomarker of EVs originating from injured cardiomyocytes. In a porcine CRS1 model, plasma levels of TRIM72 positive-EVs were increased, and we demonstrate their delivery to the kidney. Similarly, in CRS1 patients, higher plasma levels of TRIM72-positive EVs correlated with the development of acute kidney injury. Mechanistically, uptake of H-EVs by proximal tubular epithelial cells induced transcription of lipogenic genes and caused lipid accumulation, whereas lipogenesis blockade protected these cells from H-EV-induced injury. We subsequently found that reduced expression of the transcription factor FOXO3 drove H-EV-induced transcriptomic reprogramming. H-EV cargo was enriched with specific Foxo3-targeting miRNAs, whose delivery promoted proximal tubular epithelial cell cytotoxicity, oxidative stress, and suppressed FOXO3 levels. CONCLUSIONS: Overall, this work demonstrates that a Foxo3-targeting miRNA heart-to-kidney signal mediated by injured cardiac-derived EVs contributes to kidney injury in CRS1.

title: Lipoprotein(a)-dependent cardiovascular risk in different populations: are thresholds the same?
authors: Brett Stephen Mansfield; Frederick Johan Raal; Petri T. Kovanen; Alpo F. Vuorio
abstract: BACKGROUND: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is a genetically determined, independent and causal risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) and aortic stenosis. Large prospective cohort studies together with Mendelian Randomization studies have established its role in cardiovascular risk which has led to the introduction of screening and the development of Lp(a)-lowering therapies. However, interpretation of Lp(a) results in clinical practice remains a challenge, particularly across populations with significantly different baseline levels. DISCUSSION: Lp(a) levels vary according to ancestry. People of African ancestry having the highest median Lp(a) levels, followed by people from South Asia, East Asia and Europe, respectively. However, despite these differences, current Lp(a) risk thresholds are derived from populations of predominantly European ancestry and broadly applied across underrepresented population groups.Available evidence from multi-ancestry cohort studies have shown that while proportional risk for ASCVD may be similar across ancestries, the absolute risk associated with specific thresholds may differ. The application of a universal threshold may lead to over-classification of risk in some populations, resulting in unnecessary edicalization and strain on healthcare systems. Conversely, some populations may be under-classified by a universal threshold potentially resulting in avoidable ASCVD events. CONCLUSION: This commentary explores the epidemiological, biological and methodological factors underlying variability in Lp(a) levels and their association with ASCVD across populations. We discuss the advantages and limitations of applying ancestry-specific Lp(a) risk thresholds. Lp(a) measurements in clinical practice should be interpreted in within a broader clinical and population context rather than in isolation.

title: Interventricular septal thickness for cardiomyopathic phenotype enrichment in patients with established left ventricular hypertrophy
authors: Wei-Ting Wang; Hui Chen; Wen-Chung Yu
journal: The International Journal of Cardiovascular Imaging
abstract: We evaluated whether interventricular septal thickness in diastole (IVSd) ≥ 15 mm enriches cardiomyopathic phenotypes among adults with established left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) and whether broader clinical-echocardiographic features improve triage. We studied 1,127 adults undergoing echocardiography from 2017 to 2019 who met established LVH criteria (sex-specific left ventricular mass index elevation and both IVSd and posterior wall thickness ≥ 13 mm). The primary phenotype was hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, Fabry disease, or amyloidosis. The composite phenotype occurred in 108 patients (9.6%) and was more frequent with IVSd ≥ 15 mm than 13.0-14.9 mm (16.2% vs. 3.6%, p < 0.001). After adjustment, IVSd ≥ 15 mm remained associated with the composite phenotype (odds ratio 2.38, 95% CI 1.35-4.20), with a graded association per 1-mm increase (odds ratio 1.50, 95% CI 1.33-1.70). At 15 mm, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, and negative predictive value were 80.6%, 55.7%, 16.2%, and 96.4%; at 18 mm, case-finding yield increased to 41.7% but 58 of 108 cases were missed. A five-variable model improved discrimination over IVSd alone (area under the curve [AUC] 0.839 vs. 0.787; ΔAUC 0.052; p = 0.007; derivation AUC 0.857, temporal validation AUC 0.788), whereas adding binary IVSd ≥ 15 mm to conventional clinical-echocardiographic variables yielded minimal incremental discrimination (ΔAUC 0.003) and minimal additional net benefit. In established LVH, IVSd ≥ 15 mm identifies cardiomyopathic enrichment, with the composite association driven predominantly by hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, but is best used as a prompt for etiologic review rather than a diagnostic rule. A compact five-variable model may support triage.

title: Impact of the COVID-19 Pandemic on Drug Utilization Patterns and Adverse Event Profiles in Cardiac Units
journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
abstract: Background: The global COVID-19 pandemic, which disproportionately affected cardiovascular patients, changed hospital processes, treatment goals, and pharmaceutical use.Preexisting illnesses and regular medication use put cardiac patients at risk.To improve medication safety and pharmacovigilance, we must understand how the pandemic affects cardiac prescriptions and ADEs.This is crucial in resource-constrained peri-urban healthcare.Method: This observational retrospective study was conducted at a secondary care hospital in Gurugram, Haryana, from 2020 to 2022.One hundred cardiac inpatients met the inclusion criteria.Hospital pharmacy data and patient papers provided demographics, medical diagnoses, prescriptions, and adverse drug event reports.Drug use patterns were examined using WHO's Anatomical Therapeutic Chemical (ATC) approach.Statistical analysis using SPSS included descriptive statistics, Chi-square tests, and t-tests with a significance level of p < 0.05.Results: The most prescribed medicines were antiplatelets (92%), statins (88%), ACE inhibitors/ARBs (76%), beta-blockers (70%), and anticoagulants (62%).Most likely due to altered COVID-19 therapeutic guidelines, anticoagulant use rose from 48% to 78% and corticosteroid use from 8% to 34%.ADEs affected 27% of patients, or 27/100.Blood loss (7%), hypotension (5%), and myalgia (4%) were the most common adverse medication events.COVID-positive cardiac patients reported 39.3% adverse medication events compared to 22.2%, suggesting a higher pharmacological risk due to advanced pandemic treatment regimens.Conclusion: The COVID-19 pandemic made managing cardiovascular sickness and infection-related comorbidities more difficult, changing cardiac inpatient drug utilisation and adverse drug event profiles.Since anticoagulants and corticosteroids were more common, medication-related problems increased.The findings emphasise the necessity of continuous cardiac monitoring, acceptable prescribing rules, and strong pharmacovigilance systems in peri-urban secondary care institutions.Future multicentric trials should corroborate these trends and establish the framework for real-time adverse medication event monitoring in post-pandemic cardiac therapy.

title: The diagnostic value of admission myoglobin for sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy: a prospective cohort study
authors: Yue Chen; Xiaohong Lin; Guangwei Yu
abstract: Background Sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy (SICM) is a frequent and under-recognized complication of sepsis. Early diagnosis remains challenging. We evaluated the diagnostic value of admission myoglobin (MYO), alone and combined with NT-proBNP and the SOFA score, for SICM in patients with sepsis. Methods In this single-center prospective cohort study (April 2022 to May 2024), we enrolled 158 patients with sepsis diagnosed according to Sepsis-3 criteria. Blood samples for MYO and NT-proBNP were collected within 24 h of admission; admission echocardiography was performed as soon as feasible (within 24 h whenever possible, and within 72 h in all enrolled patients); follow-up echocardiography was performed between day 7 and day 14. SICM was defined as left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) below 50% with documented reversibility. Univariate and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors associated with SICM, adjusting for age, sex, body mass index, and renal function. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis, internal validation by 1,000 bootstrap resamples, and decision curve analysis (DCA) were performed. Model calibration was assessed by a calibration plot, the calibration intercept and slope, and the Brier score, with bootstrap optimism-corrected estimates. Results Of 158 patients, 63 (39.9%) were diagnosed with SICM. MYO levels were significantly higher in the SICM group than in the non-SICM group (median 395.7 vs. 97.3 ng/mL, P < 0.001). In multivariate analysis adjusting for age, sex, BMI, and renal function, MYO (OR 1.061 per 100 ng/mL, 95% CI 1.008–1.115; P = 0.023) and NT-proBNP (OR 1.087 per 1,000 pg/mL, 95% CI 1.025–1.153; P = 0.005) were independently associated with SICM. The combined model (MYO + NT-proBNP + SOFA) achieved an area under the ROC curve (AUC) of 0.821 (95% CI: 0.750–0.892), outperforming SOFA alone (AUC 0.743; likelihood ratio test P < 0.001); the optimism-corrected AUC after bootstrap validation was 0.812. The model was well calibrated (calibration intercept 0.00, slope 1.00; Brier score 0.173). DCA suggested potential net benefit across threshold probabilities of 0.1–0.7. Conclusion Admission MYO, particularly in combination with NT-proBNP and SOFA, may assist in the early identification and diagnosis of SICM.

title: Left Atrial Appendage Closure Versus Oral Anticoagulation for Prevention of Stroke or Systemic Embolism in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation: An Updated Meta‐Analysis of 7004 Patients Across Six Randomized Trials
authors: Aymen Bushra Ahmed; Neha Saleem Paryani; Muteia Shakoor; Vikash Jaiswal; Harsh Golwala; Jonathan R. Rosenberg; Mark D. Metzl; Mark J. Ricciardi; Gregory Y. H. Lip; Arman Qamar
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) is an emerging alternative for stroke prevention in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) who are unsuitable for long-term oral anticoagulants (OACs). However, its efficacy and safety relative to OACs remain uncertain. METHODS: Three databases were searched up to April 7, 2026, for randomized controlled trials comparing LAAC with OAC in patients with AF. Risk ratios with 95% confidence intervals were pooled using a random-effects model. RESULTS: Six RCTs (n = 7004 patients) were analyzed. The risk of stroke or systemic embolism (SSE) did not differ significantly between the LAAC and OAC groups (RR: 1.10 [0.87-1.39]; p = 0.42). The risk of ischemic SSE was significantly increased with LAAC (RR: 1.41 [1.07-1.85]; p = 0.02) compared with OAC. No significant differences were observed in all-cause mortality (RR: 0.94 [0.81-1.09]), cardiovascular mortality (RR: 0.91 [0.69-1.21]), non-cardiovascular mortality (RR: 0.91 [0.75-1.12]), or hemorrhagic stroke (RR: 0.58 [0.29-1.17]). LAAC was associated with a similar risk of overall major bleeding (RR: 0.92 [0.77-1.09]) and low risk of non-procedural bleeding (RR: 0.61 [0.52-0.73]; p < 0.001) compared with OAC. Upon sensitivity analysis comparing LAAC with DOACs, the findings remained consistent across most clinical outcomes. CONCLUSION: LAAC demonstrates comparable risks of SSE and major bleeding to OACs, but is associated with a higher risk of ischemic SSE and reduced non-procedural bleeding, supporting its use in selected patients at high risk for long-term bleeding while emphasizing individualized shared decision-making.

title: Long‐term outcomes following modified Blalock–Taussig–Thomas shunt placement in 13 dogs with cyanotic congenital heart disease
authors: Matteo Rossanese; Joshua Hannabuss; Daniel J. Brockman
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To describe long-term outcome and owner-perceived quality of life in dogs with cyanotic congenital cardiac disease undergoing modified Blalock-Taussig-Thomas shunt procedure. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Medical records of dogs that underwent Blalock-Taussig-Thomas shunt between 2009 and 2025 at a small animal referral hospital were retrospectively reviewed. Complications, long-term outcomes and quality of life were assessed via clinical examination and/or contact with owners or referring veterinarians. RESULTS: Thirteen dogs were included. The predominant clinical signs were exercise intolerance, cyanosis and a heart murmur. Diagnosis included tetralogy of Fallot (n = 8), double outlet right ventricle (n = 3); tetralogy of Fallot-double outlet right ventricle spectrum (n = 1) and tetralogy of Fallot with pulmonary atresia spectrum (n = 1). All dogs survived surgery. Follow-up was available for 12 dogs, ranging from 58 to 2094 days. Eight dogs died or were euthanased for cardiac-related reasons, three were alive at follow-up and one dog was alive 278 days after surgery at last point of contact. All dogs showed a marked postoperative clinical improvement. Shunt obstruction or partial obstruction was documented in three of 12 dogs at 265, 587 and 693 days. Postoperative balloon valvuloplasty was performed in three of the 12 dogs, one died during the procedure and two dogs showed clinical improvement and extended good quality survival. Owners' perception of the procedure outcome and quality of life was described as good, with only mild adjustments needed for exercise. CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE: Blalock-Taussig-Thomas shunt is an effective palliative option for dogs with cyanotic congenital cardiac diseases associated with reduced pulmonary blood flow, providing sustained clinical improvement and quality of life. Recurrence of clinical signs could indicate shunt obstruction and warrants prompt assessment.
